issues.quote: Power in a medium is $P = n_{medium}/f$.
issues.problem: This is not the NCERT definition of power. NCERT uses $P = 1/f$ throughout. The change of power in a liquid already comes from the lens maker's formula through $n_{21}$. The extra factor contradicts the formula given in the same topic and in the formula sheet. A student who also applies $n_{21}$ would count the medium twice in lens-in-liquid questions.
issues.correction: Power is $P = 1/f$ (f in metres). In a medium, find the new f from the lens maker's formula with $n_{21} = n_{lens}/n_{medium}$, then take $P = 1/f$.

issues.quote: parallel to the base for an equilateral prism
issues.problem: This suggests the ray travels parallel to the base only in an equilateral prism. At minimum deviation, $r_1 = r_2 = A/2$, so the ray inside is parallel to the base for any isosceles prism. It is not parallel for every prism shape.
issues.correction: At minimum deviation the ray passes symmetrically through the prism. Inside an isosceles (including equilateral) prism, it travels parallel to the base.
